images.title: General (Head-to-Toe) Examination
images.must_show: Conjunctival pallor: lower eyelid everted in a patient with anaemia, alongside a normal comparator
images.point: Conjunctival pallor is one of the few bedside signs of anaemia usable across all skin tones
images.alt: Conjunctival pallor: lower eyelid everted in a patient with anaemia, alongside a normal comparator

images.title: General (Head-to-Toe) Examination
images.must_show: Scleral icterus in natural daylight, with a normal comparator
images.point: Jaundice is detected in the sclera before the skin, and artificial light masks it
images.alt: Scleral icterus in natural daylight, with a normal comparator

images.title: General (Head-to-Toe) Examination
images.must_show: Finger clubbing shown in profile with the Schamroth window test
images.point: Clubbing is graded and the Schamroth window is the most reproducible bedside demonstration
images.alt: Finger clubbing shown in profile with the Schamroth window test

images.title: General (Head-to-Toe) Examination
images.must_show: Koilonychia and leukonychia side by side
images.point: Two nail signs pointing to entirely different deficiencies — iron versus albumin
images.alt: Koilonychia and leukonychia side by side

images.title: General (Head-to-Toe) Examination
images.must_show: Demonstration of pitting oedema: thumb pressure held over the tibia and the resulting pit
images.point: Technique matters — pressure must be held long enough or pitting is missed
images.alt: Demonstration of pitting oedema: thumb pressure held over the tibia and the resulting pit

images.title: General (Head-to-Toe) Examination
images.must_show: Cervical lymph node chains marked on a neck
images.point: A systematic order prevents nodes being missed
images.alt: Cervical lymph node chains marked on a neck

images.title: Cardiovascular System Examination
images.must_show: Anterior chest wall with the four auscultation areas marked on surface anatomy
images.point: Correct surface anatomy is the difference between hearing and missing a murmur
images.alt: Anterior chest wall with the four auscultation areas marked on surface anatomy

images.title: Cardiovascular System Examination
images.must_show: Correct JVP assessment: patient at 45°, head turned, with the vertical height above the sternal angle marked
images.point: The JVP is measured vertically from the sternal angle, not along the neck
images.alt: Correct JVP assessment: patient at 45°, head turned, with the vertical height above the sternal angle marked

images.title: Cardiovascular System Examination
images.must_show: Stethoscope bell and diaphragm shown side by side with their frequency use
images.point: Using the wrong side is one of the commonest reasons murmurs are missed
images.alt: Stethoscope bell and diaphragm shown side by side with their frequency use

images.title: Cardiovascular System Examination
images.must_show: Left lateral decubitus position for the mitral stenosis murmur, and sitting-forward position for aortic regurgitation
images.point: These manoeuvres are what make quiet diastolic murmurs audible
images.alt: Left lateral decubitus position for the mitral stenosis murmur, and sitting-forward position for aortic regurgitation

images.title: Cranial Nerve Examination — All Twelve
images.must_show: Base of skull with the twelve cranial nerve foramina labelled
images.point: Foramen anatomy explains which nerves are affected together in skull base pathology
images.alt: Base of skull with the twelve cranial nerve foramina labelled

images.title: Cranial Nerve Examination — All Twelve
images.must_show: Upper motor neurone versus lower motor neurone facial palsy, both attempting to raise the eyebrows
images.point: Forehead sparing is the single most important discriminator — stroke versus Bell palsy
images.alt: Upper motor neurone versus lower motor neurone facial palsy, both attempting to raise the eyebrows

images.title: Cranial Nerve Examination — All Twelve
images.must_show: Visual field defects mapped against lesion site along the visual pathway
images.point: The field defect localises the lesion precisely
images.alt: Visual field defects mapped against lesion site along the visual pathway

images.title: Cranial Nerve Examination — All Twelve
images.must_show: Rinne and Weber test technique and interpretation table
images.point: These two simple tests separate conductive from sensorineural loss at the bedside
images.alt: Rinne and Weber test technique and interpretation table

images.title: Cranial Nerve Examination — All Twelve
images.must_show: Third nerve palsy showing ptosis, dilated pupil and the 'down and out' eye
images.point: A painful pupil-involving third nerve palsy is an aneurysm until excluded
images.alt: Third nerve palsy showing ptosis, dilated pupil and the 'down and out' eye

images.title: Neurological Power, Tone and Reflex Grading
images.must_show: Correct tendon hammer technique for biceps, supinator, triceps, knee and ankle reflexes
images.point: Poor technique is the commonest reason a present reflex appears absent
images.alt: Correct tendon hammer technique for biceps, supinator, triceps, knee and ankle reflexes

images.title: Neurological Power, Tone and Reflex Grading
images.must_show: Correct path for eliciting the plantar response
images.point: Stimulating the wrong part of the sole produces a withdrawal response mistaken for Babinski
images.alt: Correct path for eliciting the plantar response

images.title: Neurological Power, Tone and Reflex Grading
images.must_show: Dermatome map, anterior and posterior
images.point: Sensory level determination depends on an accurate dermatome map
images.alt: Dermatome map, anterior and posterior

images.title: Neurological Power, Tone and Reflex Grading
images.must_show: Myotome chart matched to the movements used to test them
images.point: Recording the myotome rather than 'weak limb' localises the lesion
images.alt: Myotome chart matched to the movements used to test them

images.title: Blood Collection Tubes — Colour Code Reference
images.must_show: Full set of blood collection tubes photographed together in the correct order of draw, stoppers clearly visible
images.point: Recognising the tube by colour at a glance prevents the wrong sample being sent and repeated venepuncture
images.alt: A row of blood collection tubes arranged left to right in order of draw, each with a differently coloured stopper

images.title: Blood Collection Tubes — Colour Code Reference
images.must_show: Correctly filled versus under-filled light blue citrate tube, with the fill line marked
images.point: An under-filled citrate tube produces a falsely prolonged INR and can trigger inappropriate treatment
images.alt: Correctly filled versus under-filled light blue citrate tube, with the fill line marked

images.title: Blood Collection Tubes — Colour Code Reference
images.must_show: Order-of-draw sequence chart with the carryover risk annotated at each step
images.point: Explains WHY the order matters rather than asking staff to memorise it
images.alt: Order-of-draw sequence chart with the carryover risk annotated at each step

images.title: Blood Collection Tubes — Colour Code Reference
images.must_show: Correct gentle inversion technique for mixing an EDTA tube
images.point: Shaking haemolyses; failing to mix clots. Both waste the sample.
images.alt: Correct gentle inversion technique for mixing an EDTA tube

images.title: Airway, Tubes and Catheters — Identification, Sizing and Indications
images.must_show: Peripheral cannulae laid out by colour with the gauge number labelled beside each
images.point: The colour-gauge relationship must be instant knowledge in an emergency
images.alt: Six intravenous cannulae arranged by size, each a different colour, labelled with their gauge

images.title: Airway, Tubes and Catheters — Identification, Sizing and Indications
images.must_show: The safe triangle for chest drain insertion marked on a torso
images.point: Insertion outside the safe triangle risks injury to the liver, spleen, heart and long thoracic nerve
images.alt: The safe triangle for chest drain insertion marked on a torso

images.title: Airway, Tubes and Catheters — Identification, Sizing and Indications
images.must_show: Cross-section of a rib showing the neurovascular bundle in the subcostal groove, with the correct 'over the top of the rib' needle path
images.point: Explains why the tube passes above the rib and not below it
images.alt: Cross-section of a rib showing the neurovascular bundle in the subcostal groove, with the correct 'over the top of the rib' needle path

images.title: Airway, Tubes and Catheters — Identification, Sizing and Indications
images.must_show: Endotracheal, tracheostomy, nasogastric and urinary catheters photographed side by side with a scale ruler
images.point: Recognising each device on sight prevents dangerous misidentification at the bedside
labels: ETT with cuff and pilot balloon
images.alt: Endotracheal, tracheostomy, nasogastric and urinary catheters photographed side by side with a scale ruler

images.title: Airway, Tubes and Catheters — Identification, Sizing and Indications
images.must_show: Oropharyngeal airway sizing measured from incisors to angle of jaw
images.point: A wrongly sized airway worsens obstruction
images.alt: Oropharyngeal airway sizing measured from incisors to angle of jaw

images.title: Airway, Tubes and Catheters — Identification, Sizing and Indications
images.must_show: Correct and incorrect nasogastric tube positions on chest radiograph
images.point: Feeding through a misplaced tube is a never event
images.alt: Correct and incorrect nasogastric tube positions on chest radiograph

images.title: Surgical Instruments — Recognition and Use by Function
images.must_show: Instrument tray photographed from above with each instrument numbered and keyed
images.point: Recognising the standard tray layout speeds theatre work and reduces asking
images.alt: Instrument tray photographed from above with each instrument numbered and keyed

images.title: Surgical Instruments — Recognition and Use by Function
images.must_show: Close-up comparison of Allis versus Babcock forceps tips
images.point: The single most commonly confused pair; the tips are unmistakable when seen side by side
images.alt: Close-up comparison of Allis versus Babcock forceps tips

images.title: Surgical Instruments — Recognition and Use by Function
images.must_show: Close-up comparison of Mayo versus Metzenbaum scissors showing the shank-to-blade ratio
images.point: Using tissue scissors to cut suture blunts them and is a common theatre error
images.alt: Close-up comparison of Mayo versus Metzenbaum scissors showing the shank-to-blade ratio

images.title: Surgical Instruments — Recognition and Use by Function
images.must_show: Kocher forceps tip showing the interlocking tooth, beside a Spencer Wells tip without one
images.point: The tooth is what makes Kocher secure and traumatic
images.alt: Kocher forceps tip showing the interlocking tooth, beside a Spencer Wells tip without one

images.title: Surgical Instruments — Recognition and Use by Function
images.must_show: Scalpel blade shapes 10, 11, 15, 20 and 22 shown to scale
images.point: Blade selection depends on the incision; the No. 11 stab blade is distinct
images.alt: Scalpel blade shapes 10, 11, 15, 20 and 22 shown to scale

images.title: Surgical Instruments — Recognition and Use by Function
images.must_show: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist three-phase poster
images.point: The checklist is a mandated safety control, not an optional formality
images.alt: WHO Surgical Safety Checklist three-phase poster

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: Normal PA chest radiograph with anatomical structures labelled
images.point: A confident model of normal is a prerequisite for detecting abnormality
images.alt: Normal PA chest radiograph with anatomical structures labelled

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: RIPE quality assessment demonstrated on annotated films
images.point: Interpreting a technically inadequate film produces false findings
images.alt: RIPE quality assessment demonstrated on annotated films

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: Erect chest radiograph showing free air under the right hemidiaphragm
images.point: The single most important emergency finding on an erect chest film
images.alt: Erect chest radiograph showing free air under the right hemidiaphragm

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: Pneumothorax with the visceral pleural line marked, alongside a normal comparator
images.point: The pleural line is subtle and is missed unless specifically traced
labels: absent lung markings beyond the line
images.alt: Pneumothorax with the visceral pleural line marked, alongside a normal comparator

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: Lobar consolidation demonstrating the silhouette sign at the right heart border
images.point: The silhouette sign localises disease without needing a lateral film
images.alt: Lobar consolidation demonstrating the silhouette sign at the right heart border

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: Pleural effusion with meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle
images.point: Blunting of the costophrenic angle is the earliest radiographic sign of effusion
images.alt: Pleural effusion with meniscus sign and blunted costophrenic angle

images.title: Chest Radiograph — Systematic Interpretation
images.must_show: Correct and incorrect endotracheal and nasogastric tube positions on chest radiograph
images.point: Device position review is part of every chest film read in a ward or ICU patient
labels: NG tube below diaphragm in midline
images.alt: Correct and incorrect endotracheal and nasogastric tube positions on chest radiograph

images.title: Finger Clubbing — Grading and Causes
images.must_show: Normal finger profile beside grade 3–4 clubbing, both in lateral view
images.point: The Lovibond angle change is best appreciated in profile against a normal comparator
images.alt: Normal finger profile beside grade 3–4 clubbing, both in lateral view

images.title: Finger Clubbing — Grading and Causes
images.must_show: Schamroth window test: normal diamond window and obliterated window side by side
images.point: This is the most reproducible bedside demonstration of clubbing
images.alt: Schamroth window test: normal diamond window and obliterated window side by side

images.title: Diabetic Foot — Risk Stratification and Examination
images.must_show: The 10 g monofilament testing sites marked on a plantar surface diagram
images.point: Testing the wrong sites gives a false-negative neuropathy screen
labels: sites to avoid: callus and ulcer
images.alt: The 10 g monofilament testing sites marked on a plantar surface diagram

images.title: Diabetic Foot — Risk Stratification and Examination
images.must_show: Correct monofilament technique showing buckling of the filament
images.point: The filament must buckle; pressing harder invalidates the test
images.alt: Correct monofilament technique showing buckling of the filament

images.title: Diabetic Foot — Risk Stratification and Examination
images.must_show: Charcot foot with rocker-bottom deformity, beside an early red hot swollen Charcot foot
images.point: Early Charcot foot looks like cellulitis; recognising it before collapse prevents amputation
labels: erythema and swelling without proportionate pain
images.alt: Charcot foot with rocker-bottom deformity, beside an early red hot swollen Charcot foot

images.title: Diabetic Foot — Risk Stratification and Examination
images.must_show: Wagner grades 1 to 5 illustrated
images.point: Consistent grading drives referral urgency and treatment choice
images.alt: Wagner grades 1 to 5 illustrated

images.title: Diabetic Foot — Risk Stratification and Examination
images.must_show: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulse locations marked on the foot
images.point: These pulses are frequently sought in the wrong place and wrongly recorded as absent
labels: dorsalis pedis — lateral to extensor hallucis longus tendon
images.alt: Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulse locations marked on the foot
